decisions.reason: Although it builds directly on our radiant-heating know-how, its disappearance from the website by 2024 suggests our early learning showed too little standalone commercial value to justify continued resource commitment.

The electric infrared panel heater was close enough for us to test, but its rapid removal from the website indicates weak market traction and a less distinctive fit with our core large-space system capabilities than our established solutions.

Despite leveraging related infrared knowledge, the electric halogen variant appears not to have generated sufficient results after launch, so absorptive learning argues for redirecting effort to more promising and better-fitting developments.

The hydrogen-capable gas dark infrared heater closely matches our existing knowledge base and strategic move toward lower-carbon heating, and the stronger 2024 positioning after a real-world 2023 deployment shows we can absorb feedback and improve it commercially.
